Every entry below was MEASURED. A claim with no measurement does not belong here.

verified.fact: Rotations interpolate with slerp everywhere; there are no raw quaternion lerps in the bake or retarget.
verified.evidence: scripts/audit-quaternion-paths.mjs — 1,570 hemisphere flips exist across 255 of 455 clips and are harmless because THREE.Quaternion.slerp corrects the sign.

verified.fact: Cancel windows open at 0.20 of the move.
verified.evidence: Median of 213 windows authored across 133 imported Schwarzerblitz moves.

verified.fact: The live rendered bodies carry ZERO cross-body skin weights.
verified.evidence: scripts/probe-live-skin.mjs — WRECK 0/12,035 and TITAN 0/11,469 in a real match.

verified.fact: WRECK_PATTERSON's rig is indistinguishable from VIPER's, which was never reported.
verified.evidence: Bone-SEGMENT distance medians 16.9cm vs 17.1cm. Measuring to the joint ORIGIN instead over-reports long bones and was the source of an earlier wrong claim.

verified.fact: A fighter crosses 1.23 of his own strike reaches per second of walking, matching Schwarzerblitz.
verified.evidence: 80 units/s over a 65-unit modal range there; 1.72 m/s over a measured 1.40m reach here.

verified.fact: A jab connects out to 1.40m — measured, not assumed.
verified.evidence: src/engine/locomotion/pace.test.ts drives a real attack to its furthest connecting distance.

verified.fact: Linear blend skinning collapses the thigh to 0.29-0.49 of its radius at 180 degrees of twist, on every model including the best rig shipped.
In real clips the thigh pinches to a median 0.68 and as low as 0.23 of bind radius; dual quaternion skinning roughly doubles what is retained but does not fully fix it (0.23 -> 0.42).
verified.evidence: tools/model_diag/lbs_in_play.mjs, validated on TPOSE=1.000 and GRAFQUICKJAB=1.000 before being trusted.

verified.fact: The thigh sits a median 81 degrees from its bind across 455 clips, and 126 degrees is the joint limiter (bend 120 / twist 50) working as designed, not corruption.
verified.evidence: tools/model_diag/rest_offset.mjs; only 17 clips are a pure stuck offset, so this is a systematic baseline from rest-pose mismatch rather than a few bad files.

verified: A punch really does rotate the pelvis past a right angle. ALTERNATINGFOREARMS' pelvis, frame by frame away from its own first frame: 0 10 11 30 33 32 46 71 100 84 40 10 38 76 103 102 112 111 101 121 108 105 101 101. Peaks at 121 and ends 101 out. CHOKESLAM ends 117 out, DDT 86. IDLE sways to 55 and returns to 0.

SPEED, not size, separates a real leg track from a corrupt one. HURRICANE_KICK is a real kick capture and its fastest lower-body joint peaks at 786 deg/s; ALTERNATINGFOREARMS moves its THIGH at 998. 190 of 455 clips are past the bank's own fastest kick or fail to return the pelvis to a stance.

Masking the legs off a hand strike takes the pelvis from 94.6 degrees outside the idle stance to 7.2, measured through the real controller on the real clip, with the same clip played as a kick as the in-run control (tools/parity/pelvis_gate.ts).

THREE.AnimationMixer has no per-bone evaluate loop, so a bone mask is a TRACK SPLIT plus a second action, not a `continue`. The mixer accumulates per binding: a bone with no track in any playing action is never written, so the stance clip's lower half can own the pelvis while the strike owns the arms.

THE CANDY WRAPPER WAS MOSTLY THE DATA, NOT LINEAR BLEND SKINNING. Holding the legs at the stance takes the thigh radius from 0.65 median to 0.92 across 60 real clips, and 0 of them pinch below 0.85 where 40 did. ALTERNATINGFOREARMS: 0.23 -> 0.92. DQS on the same clip only reaches 0.42, so the shader would have been the expensive fix for a data problem.

What real LBS loss remains is narrow and measured: clips that are CREDIBLE and genuinely extreme — BREAKDANCE_FREEZES 0.41, CAPOEIRA 0.25 with a clean pelvis. DQS roughly doubles those (0.25 -> 0.48) without fixing them. That, and full-body clips whose legs are corrupt and cannot be masked because the legs ARE the move (APRONJAYKICK leaves the pelvis 92 deg out).

Every basic attack was a multi-second combination clip. attack_1 played BOXING 1.733s striking backward (fwd -0.999), attack_rp COMBO_PUNCH 2.967s (fwd -1.000), attack_lk DROP_KICK 2.900s at spineUp 0.655, attack_rk HURRICANE_KICK 1.833s and frozen. Now GRAFQUICKJAB 0.458s, UPPERCUT 0.417s, QUICKKICK 0.250s, HEAVYKICK 0.542s.
crouchLightAttack and crouchHeavyAttack had frame data, alias lists and a semantic mapping, and no input path in FighterStateMachine ever entered either. Down+kick gave the STANDING kick, measured.

Grok's meshopt pass on the models is lossless on 15 of 17: identical triangles, identical joints and morphs, every UV seam intact, 10.2 MB saved (JAGER 4696->2956KB, TARZANIAN_DEVIL 3867->1347KB, CODY_gear 1813->708KB). The two rejects, MAIME_skinned and MAIME_tattered_skinned, had TEXCOORD_0 REMOVED — seams 2954->0 and 1011->0.

React could not install and rocket-update's report was accurate: react 19.3.0 is published, our range was ^19.2.0, and @react-three/fiber@9.7.0 declares react >=19 <19.3. The lockfile's 19.2.8 was the only thing holding it together. Fixed by narrowing our range, not by overriding fiber's peer declaration.

brutalfist11's BAKE is a regression on the 18 clips where it really differs, measured on the credibility gate: HIT_TO_BODY 289 -> 3021 deg/s, CENTER_BLOCK 215 -> 2060, DRUNK_RUN_FORWARD 477 -> 1990, ILLEGAL_KNEE 423 -> 1611. Ours wins 12, theirs 0, 3 ties; 190 non-credible clips against their 200. Its clips were NOT taken, and its .json.zst files were not either — the zstd pack was regenerated from our own bake.

BASELINE PARITY, first measured: 76% across 36 rows, now 79% — TIMEBASE 100, INPUT 100, ANIMATION 100, FRAME DATA 88, MECHANICS 69, FEEL 50. 24 behaving, 9 wired, 3 declared and dead, 0 missing. tools/parity/baseline.ts, gated in the critic at a 79% floor.

The biggest single gap was advantage on block: blockstun was a flat per-animation duration never compared against the attacker's recovery, so EVERY move was neutral. Now derived from an authored advantage — jab +1, light kick 0, heavy punch -9, heavy kick -10, crouch punch -3, low kick -12 — all six realising exactly what they author.

Our light punch was 7.2 frames of startup against the i10 lineage standard: too FAST, not too slow. Whole-move scale was off with it (totals 26-48 frames where a jab is ~20 and a heavy ~40). The six basics are now whole frame counts at 60fps.
BASELINE PARITY 79% -> 89%, 0 declared-and-dead rows. FRAME DATA 88->100, MECHANICS 69->83. Rage, low parry, power-crush armour and the wall-splat advantage all now BEHAVING under registered tests.

RAGE ALREADY EXISTED UNDER THE NAME `Finisher`: FINISHER_HP_THRESHOLD 0.25, FINISHER_DAMAGE 350, FINISHER_STARTUP_FRAMES 15 ('super armor startup'). That is a Rage Art. But those constants plus HEAT_ATTACKS and SUPER_ARMOR_ACTIVE_FRAMES had ZERO readers — the state was created and ticked, the numbers meant nothing. RageSystem imports them rather than declaring new ones.

SchwarzerblitzEngine's defensive design, ported: `FK_Character::hasArmor(type)` asks the MOVE at the CURRENT FRAME about a SPECIFIC ATTACK TYPE, windows stored on the move (FK_Move: armorFrames, invincibilityFrames), coverage as an attack-type bitmask with composite masks (FK_Database: HighAtks/MidAtks/LowAtks/HighAndMidAtks/AllAtk/NoType). A power crush is then a move with one window, not a system — one line on the heavy punch.

WALL_SPLAT_BONUS_FRAMES = 18, 'extra frames attacker gets to chain combo', was written into every splat by applyWallSplat and read by NOBODY. A wall carry bought no frames. registerHit now takes the defender's comboExtensionFrames and widens the combo window by it, derived from the constant.

HITSTOP WAS THREE SYSTEMS that disagreed about what a heavy hit is worth: HIT_STOP_DURATIONS in milliseconds per attack key (light 80 / heavy 140 / throw 180), hitStopFramesForImpact deriving frames from force and CLAMPING everything into 3-5 so a throw and a jab froze for nearly the same time, and inline literals in the arena (0.045 on a block, 0.06 on a parry). One table now, in frames, with block at 1/3 and parry at 1/2 of the clean hit so tuning the table tunes everything. FEEL 50% -> 100%.
traps: Measure the DENOMINATOR too. Taking the strike reach as 0.8m from a test's swing distance made a 1.28x pace gap look like 2.2x.
A joint origin sits at one END of its bone, so distance-to-origin calls a correctly weighted shin broken.
A Mixamo thigh's bind local rotation is already ~180 degrees. Absolute joint angles are meaningless; measure the delta from bind.
Swing-twist decomposition has a singularity near 180 degrees and reports a large swing as a large twist.
A test that never runs the thing it names passes for the wrong reason. Assert that the move under test actually fired.
QuaternionKeyframeTrack stores Float32 while a bone quaternion is a double, so an identical pose measures ~0.02 degrees apart.
An import that reports zero skips AND zero output is broken, not idle. Count what went IN.

Do not decide a mask by measuring the clip's own leg tracks — that is circular. The obvious rule (a large offset that barely varies is a baked-in constant) puts ALTERNATINGFOREARMS in the SAFE pile, because its legs travel 174 degrees, which reads as footwork until you see it travelled at 998 deg/s. The engine already knows better from WHAT THE PLAYER PRESSED.

A stance is an ENVELOPE, not a pose. Comparing a held pelvis with ONE frame of IDLE reported 64.5 degrees with the mask working correctly — IDLE's own pelvis sways 55 degrees, so any single frame of it is ~50 from the rest of the same clip. Measure the distance OUTSIDE every pose the stance passes through.

Advice for this engine keeps arriving in C++ because that is the language the animation literature is written in. Translate the mechanism and say what it became; never answer with 'we are not C++'. AGENTS.md carries the translation table and a line to paste at whatever keeps assuming it.

Do not gate on a number that can never go green — a permanently red gate trains everyone to ignore the critic. The hip-volume gate measures the MASKED path, which is what a hand strike plays, and PRINTS the unmasked figure beside it so the open exposure stays visible.

A gate set to catch the catastrophe misses the defect. UPRIGHT_SPINE_MIN = 0 only rejects a body that is fully upside down; what was shipping on the light kick was a body leaning 49 degrees off vertical (spineUp 0.655), which is exactly the crouch the owner reported. Set the bar where the defect is, not where the disaster is.

Never pick a basic attack by sweeping the bake on measurements. Ranked over 455 clips for upright/forward/short, the best hand strikes are ELENATHROWREACTION, TIGERSTANCE and MIRAAIRTHROWREACTION — two hit reactions and a stance. A body being thrown extends a limb forward exactly like a body punching; that is what the move-library checkboxes are for. Reorder WITHIN each slot's curated list.

A known defect parked behind 'that is a design decision' never gets decided. HURRICANE_KICK was recorded in the alias file as a frozen spinning statue and left leading the heavy kick for exactly that reason. Write the gate; the gate forces the decision.

A one-shot rAF next to a self-arming loop means the loop is dead. In CombatArena3D the hit-effect `tick` was declared and the first requestAnimationFrame was never scheduled, so four one-shot rAFs at the spawn sites were the only thing advancing the pool — one tick each, never re-armed. Count the calls; ONCE looks like working.

VERTEX COUNT IS THE WRONG MEASURE FOR A WELD. Same triangles with fewer vertices is normal deduplication. The measure that separates safe from lossy is the UV SEAM COUNT — a position carrying two texture coordinates IS a seam, and fusing it stretches the texture across the join. My first version compared against distinct (pos,normal,uv) tuples at 1e-5 and failed every file, including the four that were provably fine.

AND CHECK WHETHER THE ATTRIBUTE IS STILL THERE BEFORE CALLING IT A CLOSED SEAM. MAIME's seams read 2954 -> 0, which is too total for welding: gltfpack had pruned TEXCOORD_0 entirely because his materials reference no texture. They do not need to — his face paint is assigned IN CODE at runtime. A pruner cannot see a runtime texture.

A NEW MODULE WITH ZERO CALLERS, AGAIN. meshoptDecoderShim.ts was written to alias the worker-capable decoder over drei's synchronous copy, installAssetStream's own header claimed it was done, and nothing imported it. Also tekken-guard.test.ts and tekken-commit.test.ts were written and never added to the test script, so neither had ever run. Grep for callers on every new file in a merge.

437 of 455 clip files differed by ONE VALUE IN THE FIFTH DECIMAL (a hip position, 0.16568 vs 0.16567 = 0.01mm) and the three I sampled were byte-identical in rotation. Sampling said 'formatting noise'; scanning ALL of them found 18 clips with rotation deltas up to 1.39 and positions up to 601mm. A file-level diff count tells you nothing about which files matter — scan the whole set for the magnitude before concluding either way.
A `const` is not hoisted. Declaring FRAMES_PER_SECOND next to the blockstun code at line ~500 and calling it from a table at line ~186 is a module-init TDZ throw, not a compile error — tsc was clean.

One python replacement whose span ran from DEFAULT_MOVE_WINDOWS to a later marker silently SWALLOWED CROUCH_MOVE_WINDOWS, and the follow-up replacement then threw on a missing substring — so neither write landed while tsc still passed on the unchanged file. When replacing a span, check what else is inside it.

A pipeline's exit status is the LAST command's. `critic.mjs | tail -9 && git commit` commits even when the critic rejects, because tail exits 0. The critic caught a real tsc break and the commit went out anyway; .gitignore's `vendor/` was the only reason nothing broken reached main.

Reference code that is read rather than executed does not belong under src/ — it gets typechecked. And do not put anything you want KEPT at a path .gitignore covers: the commit that claimed to vendor a file had committed nothing, and the claim in the message was false.

PROBE THE SYSTEM, NOT THE WORD. The baseline audit searched 'Rage|rage' and reported rage MISSING while a complete health-gated super with armoured startup sat in OverdriveSystem as `Finisher`. Searching for a feature by its marketing name is the same error as classifying a move by its filename.

A defensive window starting at frame 1 leaves the move unarmoured on the frame it comes out — which is the frame a trade is most likely on. Frame 0 IS the move's first frame. Found by driving the real state machine; the resolver's own unit test had happily asserted frame 0 was closed.

Schwarzerblitz's first line in hasArmor is `if (isBeingThrown()) return false;` and that is not an edge case — a throw beating armour is what stops an armoured move being a free win. Ported deliberately.

`(key && TABLE[key]) ?? DEFAULT` returns '' for an empty-string key, not the default — `&&` yields the falsy left operand and ?? only catches null/undefined. tsc caught it as number | "". Use an explicit ternary.
